subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native trust metadata and enforcement contract should OpenClaw use for durable memory ingestion, storage, retrieval, review, and expiration?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines a security boundary, persisted state shape, plugin/API visibility, config policy, and upgrade behavior that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Native Trust Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer/security design that specifies source authority, reviewed_by semantics, trust tiers, storage-vs-influence policy, migration behavior, retrieval enforcement, and plugin exposure before code lands.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance MVP
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42647 as the prerequisite durable provenance model, then add trust tiers and policy enforcement once source lineage is settled.

options.title: Defer To External Integrations
options.body: Document external MCP/plugin memory systems such as the world-model-mcp discussion as optional solutions while explicitly leaving default OpenClaw memory without native trust enforcement for now.

recommendation.title: Design Native Trust Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer/security design that specifies source authority, reviewed_by semantics, trust tiers, storage-vs-influence policy, migration behavior, retrieval enforcement, and plugin exposure before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has prior detailed review context on this issue and strong history on the memory host/plugin seam that the product and security decision would change.
